newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares close lower in technical downturn.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares close lower in technical downturn.

text.p: Italian shares closed lower after a week of sustained rises on Friday in a technical downturn as investors took profits with Olivetti losing earlier momentum which had been spurred by talks with Germany's Mannesmann.
The all-share Mibtel index closed 0.83 percent lower at 9,977 with the blue chip Mib30 0ff 1.12 percent at 14,978.

Olivetti was one of the few major stocks to finish higher, ending 2.72 percent up at 452.6 lire. Earlier the company's shares bounded ahead when Mannesmann said talks on taking a stake in mobile phone venture Omnitel Sistemi Radiocellulari could be concluded on Friday.
Olivetti soared to a high of 483 lire on the news before easing.
Fiat shares, which have gained some 10 percent over the past week, were not spared from the bout of profit-taking, easing 1.15 percent to 4,467 lire.
The late stocks sell-off was in contrast to the performance on the bonds market which finished on a firm note, ignoring weakness in U.S. Treasuries.
Other recent gainers which went into reverse were Montedison, down 0.37 percent at 1,074 lire, Compart, down 0.71 percent at 532.2 lire and Snia, which shed 1.96 percent to close at 500 lire.
Brokers said the sell-off was sparked partly by investor reluctance to stay in the market over the weekend with uncertainty hanging over the progress through parliament of the 1997 budget.
"The market still looks in good shape but many traders don't want to hold their positions over the weekend because of the budget," said a Milan-based equities specialist. $=1,516 lire
